text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — gpu-pool-saturation detected in us-west-2 (pool: gpu-prod-4). Queue length > 6k, tail latency spiking. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale events and failed with quota/driver errors. Paging on-call: @maria-oncall.

maria-oncall: On it. Acknowledge pager. Can someone post current top errors/log snippets?

sam.driver: seeing a ton of CUDA Xid errors on a subset of nodes, looks like driver panic cycles. Example from node gpu-node-12: ```
[2026-03-15T02:12:33Z] Xid 31, pid=4021, Reason: GPU HANG
dmesg excerpt: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, PID 4021, GPU:0
NVRM: RmAccessRmInfo failed, trying reset...
```

lee-sre: confirmed. Metrics: effective GPU capacity dropped by ~42% in the last 10m due to nodes flapping. Autoscaler tried to add 6 instances but cloud returned `ResourceQuotasExceeded`. Full error: ```
error: request failed: Insufficient accelerators (requested=6, available=0)
```

maria-oncall: So two concurrent problems: driver/runtime instability causing nodes to leave the pool + quota preventing new replacements. Immediate mitigations?

sam.driver: rolling restart of the driver on affected nodes reduces Xid surge usually. I'll coordinate a canary restart on gpu-node-12 first. Command: `ssh gpu-node-12 sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` and then `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. I'll do that in 2 mins, posting status.

lee-sre: I'll put autoscaler into aggressive fallback mode to accept g4dn-slower instances (costly but avoids throttling). Trying to trigger a manual scale up with fallback instance profile. If cloud quota still denies, we need to open a provider support ticket.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: scale_attempt id=sa-8472; outcome=failed; reason=QuotaExceeded.

sam.driver: gpu-node-12 restart done. Logs show driver back up but one process crashed, restarting runtime pods. Quick health check: `nvidia-smi` shows GPU utilization back to 0 on that host.

carlos-ml: Heads up — a few production customers are reporting 503s for embedding endpoints. Telemetry shows increased 429/503 from embedding-route v2 between T-25m and now. Could be queue saturation fallback.

jane-support: I have the customer list from the support queue. Two enterprise customers (ACME Corp, StellarApps) hit timeouts and filed tickets. Marking severity P2 for now.

maria-oncall: Good. Lee, what's the ETA on fallback infra if quota is resolved?

lee-sre: If quota clears in next 15-30m, autoscaler can provision fallback pool in ~8-12m. I'm opening an expedited quota increase with cloud support now and adding an escalation tag. Ticket ID: CLD-53921 (opened).

maria-oncall: Sam, continue rolling restarts but avoid mass drains — we don't want to reduce running capacity further while the autoscaler is blocked. Prioritize nodes with highest Xid counts. Keep me posted every 5m.

sam.driver: Doing incremental restarts: nodes 12, 7, 19 so far. Node 7 shows repeated OOM killer logs hitting driver plugin: ```
Mar 15 02:18:10 gpu-node-07 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 7181 (python) score 856 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 02:18:11 gpu-node-07 nvidia-driver: GPU process 7181 triggered Xid 31
```
I suspect a memory leak in the custom runtime shim on older kernel 5.4 nodes; I recommend cordoning 07 after restart and scheduling remediation (upgrade kernel/driver).

lee-sre: Agree. I'm tagging nodes with `node-fault=driver-leak` and isolating them from the scheduler to stop new pods landing. Command run: `kubectl label node gpu-node-07 node-fault=driver-leak`.

infra-bot: autoscaler: temporary_scaling_policy=aggressive-fallback applied by lee-sre.

maria-oncall: Customer-facing status update draft? Jane, can you push a short note to the status page: "We are investigating degraded performance for embeddings in us-west-2 due to GPU node instability and scaling limits. Mitigations in progress; we will provide updates every 15 minutes."

jane-support: Posted. Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1987654321

carlos-ml: For mitigation, can we route embedding requests to CPU fallback instances at reduced concurrency/replicas? That would reduce error rates quickly even if slower. Suggestion: enable `cpu-fallback` experiment for embedding route until capacity restored.

lee-sre: Implementing now: toggling traffic-split for embedding-route v2 to send 30% to cpu-fallback pool. `kubectl apply -f traffic-split-cpu-fallback.yaml` (applied).

maria-oncall: Good. Any regressed deployments around 02:00 that could have increased memory usage?

sam.driver: Not seeing recent model changes. The common factor is older kernel/driver combos on nodes that are cycling. Looks like a latent regression with the runtime shim when OOMs occur. Will collect core dumps from 07/19 and upload to the incident S3.

lee-sre: Cloud support response: quota review queued, requested justification. I attached historical usage and upcoming incident notes. No ETA from provider yet.

pagerduty: Reminder: On-call rotation; @maria-oncall you have control until 03:00 UTC. Next oncall is @lee-sre.

maria-oncall: Acknowledged. Lee, if we don't get capacity in 30m, escalate to infra manager for emergency credits/purchase.

lee-sre: Will do. Also starting a parallel mitigation: reduce token limits and slow-rollback non-critical batch jobs to drain queue. Tagged batch jobs with `deprioritize=true`.

sam.driver: Collected a syslog + nvidia-smi dump from gpu-node-07 and uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1987654321/artifacts. Link: s3://.../gpu07-logs.tar.gz

carlos-ml: After cpu-fallback went live, 503s dropped by ~65% in 10m. Latency increased 2x for affected requests but availability improved. Telemetry: embedding-route errors from 34%->12%.

jane-support: Notified ACME and StellarApps with status update and estimated next update at +15m.

maria-oncall: Summary so far for incident timeline: - 02:12 UTC: driver Xid surge -> node flaps -> effective GPU capacity -42% - 02:20 UTC: autoscaler failed due to quota - 02:25 UTC: incremental driver restarts and node cordons - 02:30 UTC: cpu-fallback traffic split reduces customer errors. Action items: 1) Collect core dumps and logs (sam) 2) Continue node restarts and cordon affected nodes (sam/lee) 3) Pursue quota escalation with cloud (lee) 4) Customer comms (jane) 5) Post-incident: kernel/driver upgrades + runtime shim fix (owners: eng-runtime).

lee-sre: Opening follow-up RFC for kernel/driver rollout and autoscaler improvements to handle quota failures gracefully.

maria-oncall: Great. Next update in 15m or when autoscaler quota clears. If someone hits a blocking error, call page.

sam.driver: Will keep a live log in the incident doc. Currently 3 of 20 nodes cordoned, 3 restarted, 8 degraded but still serving.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: effective GPU capacity recovery to -18% (improved). Queue length decreasing. cpu-fallback handling 28% of embedding traffic.

jane-support: Updated customers with current status and provided workaround notes.

carlos-ml: Recommending a postmortem to include: longer-term fixes for driver leak, autoscaler fallback policies, pre-approved emergency quota process.

maria-oncall: Agreed. I'll keep this thread as the record. If autoscaler quota resolves, we may deprecate cpu-fallback and uncordon nodes after validation.

lee-sre: Noted. I'll escalate to infra manager if no quota change in 20m.

maria-oncall: Closing interim note — will update at 03:00 UTC or earlier. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
